note: Credit and provenance for every asset under ui/board_v2/. Kept in the same machine-readable shape as ui/assets/attribution.json and ui/assets-gothic/attribution.json, so one reader answers the licence question for any tree in this repository.
reproducibility: Two kinds of file live here and they are not equally recoverable. SCRIPT OUTPUT is regenerable: the recipe is recorded per file and was checked rather than quoted, so re-running it reproduces the committed pixels. MODEL OUTPUT is not, because the same prompt does not produce the same picture twice -- which is why every generated master is committed and kept forever, and why anything derived from one records the master it came from.
integrity: EVERY ENTRY CARRIES A sha256, present or absent, and two tests keep it that way: one asks whether a hash exists, the other whether it still matches the file. They are separate because a missing hash and a stale hash are different faults and a single test would report the wrong one. NINETY-EIGHT OF THESE WERE ADDED IN ONE PASS ON 2026-10-15, and not as a sweep of sha256sum over the tree. The gap was not a scatter of stragglers: it was whole families that earlier passes had filed without the field -- all 35 wax seals, all 35 of their masters, all 15 token files, two duty-action masters and eleven sounds. Each record was checked against its own file first, because a hash over something that contradicts its record reads as verification and is the opposite of it. That is not hypothetical here: Ordination's v02 crops described a 1065 x 522 cut while the files were 1071 x 536, and they were deliberately left unhashed rather than blessed. What was checkable was checked -- stated dimensions, every sound's duration and peak, and the seal and token geometry, where all 35 shipped seals claim a correction to 0.906 of their square and measure 0.9027 to 0.9067, all 35 masters match the pre-correction fraction their shipped record names to within 0.0006, and every stated scale factor reproduces the shipped figure. Nothing contradicted anything. WHAT A HASH HERE DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN. It identifies the bytes committed, from the date it was recorded. It cannot vouch for the file's history before that, and for the 82 entries that stated nothing checkable it is the first independent fact about the file rather than a confirmation of an old one. A re-encode also breaks it legitimately -- see sfx/README.md on ffmpeg randomising the Ogg serial number -- so a mismatch means the bytes changed, not that the sound did.

project-generated.name: Generated by a script in this repository. Nothing traced, photographed or diffused, and no model-generated content is in the file, so there is no upstream licence to honour and nothing to attribute. Where the design was arrived at with an assistant, the file's `design` note says so -- a record of how the decisions were reached, not a rights claim.

openai-generated.name: OpenAI-generated output; rights assigned to the user under the OpenAI Europe Terms of Use. Not CC0, public domain or royalty-free stock

elevenlabs-generated.name: ElevenLabs-generated audio. Section 4(c)(ii) of the Terms of Use: as between the user and ElevenLabs, the user retains all rights in their Output. COMMERCIAL USE IS TIER-DEPENDENT AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE PERMISSION HERE: section 1(c) lets a free user use the Services for non-commercial purposes ONLY, and a paid user commercially. This file was generated on a PAID plan, which is what makes it shippable; a clip generated on a free plan would not be, and the two are indistinguishable by looking at the file. Note also that ElevenLabs sublicenses SFX Outputs to other users by default unless that is disabled on the Sound Effects page, so the clip is not exclusive. Not CC0, public domain or royalty-free stock.

cc0.name: Creative Commons Zero: dedicated to the public domain. No attribution required, no restriction on commercial use or modification.

sonniss-gameaudiogdc.name: Sonniss GameAudioGDC bundle. Royalty-free for personal and commercial game use, including modification and unlimited projects, with no attribution required. The per-file `source` still names the bundle and pack: this record exists to say where a thing came from, which is a separate question from whether credit is owed.

pixabay.name: Pixabay Content License: irrevocable, worldwide, perpetual, non-exclusive and royalty-free. Commercial use and modification are permitted and no attribution is required. UNLIKE THE OTHER TWO THIRD-PARTY LICENCES HERE IT IS CONDITIONAL: the grant lapses if the file is sold or distributed on a Standalone basis -- as an audio file in substantially the form it was downloaded, including through a stock media platform. Combining it into a new creative work, which is what shipping it in the game is, is expressly not standalone use. Pixabay further disclaims any guarantee that third-party consents exist for any content, so a file carrying this licence rests on Pixabay's word rather than on a chain of title. Audio published before 9 January 2019 may instead be CC0, but the download does not say which a given file is, so nothing here claims CC0 on that basis.

provenance-pending.name: NOT A LICENCE, AND NOT A CLAIM OF ONE. A placeholder meaning the upstream permission for this file has not been supplied yet. It says only that the file is in the tree and that nobody has yet written down what may be done with it. Nothing carrying this key may be inlined into the board, and a guard enforces that; the bench plays it because the bench is a workbench. Every record using it must be resolved to a real licence before release, and the guard lists them on every run so they cannot be quietly forgotten.

assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.title: Duty wheel v2, at aspect 1.887
assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.creator: Generated by tools/ui_debug/build_duty_wheel_v2.py
assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.source: A SEPARATE BUILD, not a copy of the 1.778 baseline in tools/ui_debug/prototypes/duty_wheel_v2.svg -- that one is viewBox 1000 x 562.4 and this is 1000 x 529.9. The faces are rebuilt from the ellipse at the new aspect rather than squashed. Vendored here and read as bytes so the layout lab imports nothing from tools/ui_debug, whose builder parses argv at import time and needs numpy.
assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.design: Proportions and palette arrived at by iteration in project sessions with Claude (Anthropic): 1.887 chosen over the builder's default 1.778, the 32 degree elevation that follows from it, and the recolour from the builder's parchment into slate. The decisions were the author's. The file itself is deterministic output of the builder and contains no model-generated content -- no raster data, nothing traced or diffused, only computed vector geometry.
assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.role: the drawing the board composes the module around. generate_action_board.py reads it as bytes through geometry.WHEEL_ASSET, recolours it to slate at build time, and refuses any aspect more than 0.0005 from the design ratio. The canvas check inlines the same file through the same function.
assets/duty_wheel_v2.svg.recipe: python3 tools/ui_debug/build_duty_wheel_v2.py --aspect 1.887 --out duty_wheel_v2_1887_layout.json, then render with tools.ui_debug.render_duty_wheel_v2.render_duty_wheel_v2_svg(lay, standalone=True) from tools/ui_debug/duty_wheel_v2_1887_layout.json. See ui/board_v2/layout_lab/README.md for the exact snippet.

duty_actions/ordination/masters/ordinati.notes: master, not shipped. THE FIRST MASTER FROM THE SHARED-PIER BRIEF, which stopped asking for a wide central gutter to throw away and asked instead for one narrow masonry pier on the centre line, shared between the two cards. Three were generated in the same few minutes and all three produced the pier; this is the second (18:59), chosen on the picture over the third (19:01), which measured better on every number here. Measured and not fixed: the most vertically uniform column sits at 47.1% of the width where the seam falls at 50%, and the palette is still not honoured -- median saturation 0.180 against the 0.06-0.10 its own swatches ask for. Both are better than the Clerical master that shipped, which measures 45.3% and 0.243, and the saturated tail fell furthest: 4.1% of pixels at or above 0.30 against Clerical v03's 17.1%. SUPERSEDED BY v02 and kept anyway, per the rule for masters in this tree. Its two crops were cut, recorded and then retired unshipped when the panorama brief replaced the shared-pier one; the crops are gone, this is not.

duty_actions/ordination/masters/ordinati.notes: master, not shipped. NO DIVIDER. v01 hid the cut behind a masonry pier down the centre line, which worked and read as a contrivance. This one hides it in distance instead: an open churchyard road occupies the middle, and the seam falls in mud and puddles where there is no structure to misalign. Measured, with the caveats that matter. The seam mismatch is 35.0 at the 46th percentile of its own image, which looks poor beside v01's 28.8 at the 8th and is not comparable: that statistic ranks a cut against the quietest place available, and in an open road nowhere is quiet. Inspected at full height instead, the join is not visible. A vertical-alignment check reported a 14 px step; injecting known 4 px and 8 px steps showed the check recovers them on architecture and wanders on bare texture, so that reading is noise and nothing continuous crosses the seam here to step. Chosen on the picture over a sibling generated a minute later, which measured greyer still at 0.149. What is NOT resolved: both groups sit further out towards the edges than the brief asks, so each card carries more open ground on its inner side than v01 did. duty_actions/clerical/gain_coins/clerica.retiredNote: RETIRED 2026-10-20, replaced by clerical_gain_coins_right_v05.png -- a wider framing of the same trade, with the anvil this picture is built around replaced by a wooden workbench and the forge brought further into frame. THE REPLACEMENT TOOK TWO ATTEMPTS AND THE FIRST ONE TAUGHT THIS TREE SOMETHING ABOUT ITSELF. A v05 was offered at 1672 x 941, ratio 1.7768, where every card here is 1774 x 887 and exactly 2.0000. It was measured and refused rather than filed. The interesting part is what would have happened to it: THE RECORDS, INCLUDING THIS ONE'S OWN `modifications`, SAY AN OFF-RATIO CARD WOULD BEGIN CROPPING. IT WOULD NOT. `bundled_art()` calls `_inline()` with an explicit size and `_inline()` does `im.resize((ART_W * 2, ART_H * 2))` -- a plain resize to 988 x 494, no crop, no aspect preservation -- so the card would have been SQUASHED 11% vertically at build time, and the template's `object-fit: cover` would then have seen a 2:1 image in a 2:1 box and done nothing. The old sentence was right that no script would notice and wrong about what it would fail to notice. NOTHING IN THE TREE CHECKS A CARD'S RATIO; `geometry.ART_RATIO` is already computed as 2.0 exactly and nothing compares a picture against it.

duty_actions/clerical/gain_coins/clerica.reproducibleBy: THERE IS NO BRIEF FOR THIS PICTURE AND THERE WILL NOT BE ONE. It did not come from one prompt sent once; it came from a series of successive edit prompts in ChatGPT, and the project owner's decision on 2026-10-20 was not to document them. That is filed as a fact about this file rather than as a gap waiting to close, which is the difference between this and a `provenance-pending` key -- nothing here is outstanding. `duty_art_lab/prompts/panels/04-clerical-silversmith.md` is the brief that produced v04 and its `produces:` line still says so. It describes an earlier picture and is not this one's recipe. SO THE STANDING LINE BECOMES LOAD-BEARING. Every card record in this tree says the brief is the intent and the file is the artefact, and that the picture is committed rather than just the recipe because the same prompt does not produce the same picture twice. On the earlier cards that was an argument about fidelity. Here there is no recipe at all: these pixels cannot be made again by anyone, including the person who made them, and the committed PNG is the whole of what exists. The licence is unaffected -- ChatGPT is confirmed as the generator, which is what `openai-generated` asserts.
duty_actions/clerical/gain_coins/clerica.notes: A WIDER FRAMING OF THE SAME TRADE, and the striking surface changed under it. v04 was a tight close-up of the smith striking a die on an ANVIL, sparks flying, against a wall of hung tongs and tools; this is a wooden workbench in a vaulted room, no sparks, with the forge much larger in frame and the minted coins multiplied into stacks and two boxes. The mail-clad guard who was half cropped at v04's right edge now stands fully in frame. NOTHING FILED UNDER THIS ACTION CONTRADICTS THE CHANGE, which was worth checking rather than assuming: an anvil and a bench do not sound alike. Clerical actionB carries one bed and one cue. The bed, `silversmith_sfx_v01`, is `Fire in a Metal Stove` -- the forge, which this picture makes MORE prominent, not less. The cue is a struck bell, not a hammer on iron. So the one sound that would have cared about an anvil is not in the tree, and the one that is cares about a fire that got bigger.

sfx/buildings/scriptorium_sfx_v01.ogg.title: Scriptorium -- a pen signing
sfx/buildings/scriptorium_sfx_v01.ogg.role: the Scriptorium cue. Scriptorium adds to the acolyte total on every duty tile its owner occupies, which is a clerk's act, and a pen on paper is the plainest reading of it
sfx/buildings/scriptorium_sfx_v01.ogg.modifications: 360-1120 MS OF THE MASTER, and the choice of window is the whole of the work here. WRITING IS A TEXTURE, NOT AN EVENT -- unlike every other clip in this set it has no transient to anchor on, so what makes it identifiable is the RHYTHM of strokes rather than an attack. Cut too tight it stops being writing and becomes a scrape. This window holds four of the master's eight strokes: the long 480 ms opening stroke and then three more inside 230 ms at 20 ms spacing, which is a pen moving and cannot be read as anything else. It starts 15 ms before the pen lands, so the attack is the source's own. A 4 ms ramp in, a 35 ms fade out landing in the gap between strokes at 1108 and 1245 ms. NO DOWNMIX -- the master is mono. No level change. 44.1 kHz kept. TWO OTHER WINDOWS WERE CUT AND NOT CHOSEN: 865-1400 ms (the flurry alone, 532 ms, but it begins mid-signature and so arrives already underway) and 2010-3110 ms (ending on the master's loudest event, a 949 ms sweep, which reads as completion but is one continuous scrape rather than several strokes). Both re-cuttable from those timestamps.
sfx/buildings/scriptorium_sfx_v01.ogg.measured: 757 ms, peak -11.7 dB, mean -28.6 dB. Not clipped. Centroid 2966 Hz, 85% rolloff 6510 Hz. WHEN THIS WAS FILED IT WAS THE QUIETEST CLIP HERE BY A WIDE MARGIN, with everything else then peaking between -0.2 and -7.9 dB. Three clips have since gone lower -- Quarry -17.2, Devotion -16.4, Chapel -16.4 -- so the ranking is history and only the reason still matters. That is not a fault and no gain was applied: the master's loudness lives in its final sweep, which this window deliberately excludes. It does mean the clip will be inaudible beside the others at a shared gain and must be levelled by ear, which is the set's rule anyway and is merely more obviously true here. ITS NEAREST NEIGHBOUR IS BREWERY at 2669 Hz and 6290 -- about 300 Hz apart, the closest pair among the buildings. They are expected to separate by texture, a sustained scratch against a cork pop and slosh, but that is a listen rather than a measured fact, the same caveat recorded for Taxation against Silversmith.

sfx/buildings/inquisition_sfx_v01.ogg.modifications: UNEDITED but for the container, as asked: mono as (L+R)/2 and Vorbis q6. No trim, no fade, no level change. 96 kHz kept. THE MASTER CARRIES AN EMBEDDED PNG -- cover art as a second stream inside the WAV -- so the encode selects the audio stream explicitly rather than letting ffmpeg choose. Verified after: the shipped file holds one stream and it is Vorbis. The first file in this tree to need that. THE WIDEST STEREO SOURCE YET AND THE MOST EXPENSIVE DOWNMIX. The channels correlate at only +0.4050 -- against the foliage's 0.5349 and everything else's 0.82 to 1.0000 -- and their peaks differ by 1.9 dB (L -3.6, R -1.7), so summing costs 1.52 dB, the largest in the set against a previous worst of 1.04. Summed for the same reason as Produce Wheat: it is the convention for a genuinely stereo source, and taking one channel of a wide recording changes its character more than a decibel and a half does. Worth watching, though -- three of the last four stereo sources have been wide, and the cost is creeping up.
sfx/buildings/inquisition_sfx_v01.ogg.measured: 914 ms, peak -3.7 dB, mean -24.8 dB. Not clipped. Identity lands at -3.4 dB inside the first 150 ms; the draw runs to about 370 ms and the ring decays to -60 dB by 645. Centroid 9483 Hz, 85% rolloff 16308 Hz, both measured after resampling to 48 kHz, which truncates anything the 96 kHz master held above 24 and makes the rolloff figure a floor rather than a reading. IT IS THE BRIGHTEST OF THE METALLIC CUES and clear of all of them -- Taxation 6126, Silversmith 5170, Allocation 3290 -- so the family it looked like it would crowd is the one it avoids. ITS ACTUAL NEIGHBOUR IS BANK, the other building, at 11051 Hz with a rolloff of 16207 within 100 Hz of this one. Different sounds entirely, a blade against coins, but they occupy the same brightness and both are buildings, so that is the pair to play back to back. misc/many_coins sits at 9701 and would be closer still if it ever takes a slot.

THE LAST SECOND OF THE FILE IS DIGITAL SILENCE -- absolute zero from 46.0 s -- so the usable material is 43 to 46 s, and asking for 'the last four seconds' would have delivered a quarter of nothing. SUMMING COSTS 3.04 dB HERE, double the previous worst in this tree, and it is NOT cancellation: the channels correlate at -0.0081, which is uncorrelated rather than opposed, and -3 dB is the exact theoretical result of summing two independent signals at half amplitude. A wide cinematic mix with decorrelated reverb does this. Summed regardless, for the set's reason, but it is a third channel behaviour and sfx/README.md's table now carries a row for it. THE FADE IS 900 MS AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE WORK. The first attempt used 150 ms, which dropped 57 dB against material decaying about 1.7 dB per 100 ms on its own -- roughly twenty times steeper than the sound, and audibly cut off. The fix is not simply a longer fade: ANY fade reaching true silence is infinitely steep in dB at its end, so what decides whether a stop is heard is how loud the clip still is when that collapse happens. At 150 ms out the original sat at -28.4 dB; this one sits at -40.4. A quarter-sine curve from 700 ms. The window is unchanged -- the ending is hidden rather than the clip shortened.

sfx/buildings/quarry_sfx_v01.ogg.modifications: CUT FROM THE TAIL, NOT THE BODY. The master is 63 s and is not one recording: it is FIVE SEPARATE TAKES of about ten to twelve seconds each, divided by true digital silence at 12.7-14.0, 26.2-26.8, 36.8-38.0, 48.0-49.0 and after 61.4 s. Every take runs the same arc, a heavy crumbling body and then a tail of loose stone settling, and the five candidates auditioned were one tail from each take so that no two shared material. This is take 1's tail, 11.365 to 12.680 s of the master. Mono as (L+R)/2, resampled 96 kHz to 48, Vorbis q6. No level change. NO FADE-OUT, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE SOURCE RATHER THAN A CHOICE. The window ends 20 ms inside the library's own digital silence, so the clip stops because the recording stops; the final 150 ms measure -76.3 dB for that reason and not because anything was shaped. Three of the five candidates shared this property. Only a 4 ms declick ramp at the head, which starts at -39.7 dB mid-decay rather than from silence. THE CHEAPEST DOWNMIX IN THE TREE: channels correlate +0.8636 and their peaks differ by only 0.34 dB, so summing costs 0.43 dB against Inquisition's 1.52. Not clipped -- zero samples at full scale in either channel of the master.
sfx/buildings/quarry_sfx_v01.ogg.measured: 1315 ms, peak -17.2 dB, mean -42.4 dB. Not clipped. THE QUIETEST CLIP IN THE TREE, under Devotion's -16.4 -- which its own record did not notice, because the person filing it was looking at this file and not at the other twenty-eight. Eight discrete stones at 10, 70, 150, 270, 430, 510, 670 and 790 ms, the loudest of them -17 dB at 150 ms, so no single impact carries the clip. THIS IS THE CLIP THAT BROKE THE CENTROID AS A PROXIMITY MEASURE. Its centroid is 3733 Hz and Produce Stone's is 3674 -- 0.3 semitones apart, which would be the tightest pair in the tree and reads as a collision between the two stone cues. The band breakdown says otherwise: 62.7% of this clip's energy sits in 500-1000 Hz, while 53.7% of Produce Stone's sits in 125-250 Hz with a further 16.5% below 125. Their mass is TWO OCTAVES APART and they share a centroid only because a weighted mean of a skewed distribution does not locate that distribution. The 85% rolloff agrees with the ear instead: 1112 Hz here against 709 there, 7.8 semitones. THE 'MS' IN THE FILENAME NAMES THE MIC TECHNIQUE, NOT AN UNDECODED FILE, and the difference matters: read as raw Mid/Side and decoded, the bass would come out at -0.54 correlation, out of phase and mono-incompatible. As stored the channels correlate +0.66 below 100 Hz and near zero above, which is what a delivered spaced pair looks like, so it is used as it is. Broadband statistics cannot tell the two cases apart when the channels are decorrelated -- the M/S and L/R decompositions of independent equal-power channels are the same pair of signals -- and only the per-band reading settles it. RAIN IS THE EASIEST MATERIAL THIS TREE HAS LOOPED: the chosen start scores 0.17 dB of shoulder mismatch with 0.23 in its worst band, and even the worst candidate in the master scores 2.90. The crossfade region reads 1.24 dB under the body, and that is the material rather than the join -- the same window before any crossfade reads 1.20 dB under, so the fade accounts for 0.03. No landmark to learn: every 200 ms block sits within 2 dB of the median, and the pack is called Rain & Thunder but this file holds no thunder. Broadband the recording is calm -- 4.79 dB across 5 s blocks -- but filtered in 200 ms windows it holds thirteen events above 8 dB over their band's median, peaking at +24.4 dB at 28 s and +25.3 at 80 s, almost certainly footsteps on stone in a reverberant building. At that setting the longest event-free window in the file is 16.4 s, which caps any loop cut from it. Inside that window the best shoulder match wants an 11.5 s body: 0.91 dB RMS across five bands against 1.88 for a 14.5 s body. Re-checked against the same detector the cut reads +4.5 dB at worst, under half what was rejected. A SHORT LOOP IS THE RIGHT TRADE HERE and would not be elsewhere: this is featureless room tone with nothing to recognise, so repetition costs little, whereas one footstep every lap is a landmark. Its spectrum holds a resonance at 617 Hz sitting 12 dB above the local trend, and two copies of a tone crossfaded at arbitrary relative phase can cancel where broadband material simply sums. Candidates were scored on a narrow 550-700 Hz band alongside the usual five, and each crossfade was then built and measured rather than inferred: this one costs 0.46 dB in the howl band, and the tone across the join reads +0.07 dB against the body. Centroid 8968 Hz against the velcro rip's 8878 -- 0.2 semitones, so the brightest of the three either way -- with Silver at 7091 and Stone at 6226, and the 85% rolloff agreeing at 14732, 9811 and 13054 Hz. THE CENTROID METHOD HAD NEVER BEEN WRITTEN DOWN and was recovered by reproducing the three published figures exactly: magnitude spectrum, Hann window over the whole clip, decoded at 48 kHz. A power-weighted centroid reads 6556 here and 3700 for Stone, which is a different table and a different argument; see sfx/README.md. A QUARTER OF THE ENERGY IS BELOW 80 Hz and it is in the source, not the encode: 24.4% between 20 and 80 Hz, a body-weight thump near 30, against 0.3% between 80 and 250. It is energy and not amplitude -- high-passing at 30 Hz moves the peak by 0.02 dB -- and the K-weighting all but discards it, which is why M200 reads -22.6 on a clip whose broadband mean is -30.3.

sfx/ambient/allocation_actionA/allocatio.modifications: A SEAMLESS 28.500 s LOOP, MADE IN THE MIX RATHER THAN CUT FROM IT. Vorbis q6, 48 kHz stereo, straight from the 24-bit master: no trim, no fade, no resample, no level change. The loop was already baked when the file arrived, which is the first time that has been true here. The method is docs/ambient_composite_guide.md section 15: the finished 30 s mix has its last 1.5 s crossfaded equal-power over its first 1.5 s -- a true overlap, so the result is shorter by the crossfade and runs 28.5 s -- and is then circularly rotated so playback begins in a quiet pause. Rotation is safe only after the cycle is seamless, which is the order the guide states and the order it was done in. THE GUIDE REACHED THIS TREE'S OWN CONCLUSIONS INDEPENDENTLY. Its section 15 says not to rely on a fade to silence followed by a restart, and to bake an equal-power overlap into the asset: docs/ambient_loop_note.md sections 1 and 2, arrived at from the other direction and on different material. CHECKED RATHER THAN TRUSTED. Three laps measure identically to one pass, so the figure below describes what plays. The step across the wrap is 0.0003 in both channels, under the file's own median sample-to-sample difference. The 1.5 s window straddling the wrap sits at the 19th percentile of the loop's own 1.5 s windows -- 2.35 dB under its median, where the quietest window anywhere in the loop is 12.7 dB under it. There is no seam to find. THE SHOULDER TEST DOES NOT APPLY TO A BAKED LOOP and reads 21.5 dB here, which means nothing: comparing head and tail shoulders is how the loop note's section 5 scores a CANDIDATE, and on a file whose head has already been crossfaded with its tail it measures the material's own variation. Score candidates, not finished files. THE PREDECESSOR THIS REPLACED, NEVER COMMITTED, was a 23.510 s cut taken out of the v08 mix here rather than looped in the DAW, and it is worth a line because of what it found. v08 began and ended in digital silence, so butting it end to start made no click at all while dropping 2.5 s of near-nothing into the bed every lap -- 41.0 dB out across five bands, 68.5 dB in the top one. v09 exists because that was real. The cut also had to be an exact multiple of the key cadence, which is the finding kept in the loop note's section 9. THIS FILE'S KEY CADENCE IS NOT QUITE EVEN, and the unevenness is interior rather than at the wrap. Gaps run 3.91, 3.90, 3.92, 4.99, 3.96, 3.90 s, with the wrap landing at 3.92 and costing nothing; the odd one sits between the keys at 12.43 and 17.42 s and reads as one slower handoff rather than as a seam. The guide's section 11 plans an even four seconds, so this is the render departing from the plan, not the plan being wrong.

IT MAKES GIVE ALMS THE FIRST DUTY WITH A BED ON BOTH ITS ACTIONS -- rain over Alms, wind over Donate Building -- and the two are a pair rather than a coincidence: weather on both halves of the duty that is about giving things away. They never sound together, being different actions, but the player hears one after the other when switching, so they are levelled close on purpose: alms lands at -53.4 LUFS and this at -52.7, 0.7 dB apart. sfx/ambient/give_alms_actionB/donate_bui.modifications: A SEAMLESS 32.500 s LOOP. 32.500 s body from 64.50 s of the 215.1 s master, with the following 1.5 s folded back over the head as an equal-power crossfade. Resampled 96 -> 48 kHz on encode, Vorbis q6. No trim, no fade, no level change. THE SHOULDER SEARCH DID NOT PICK THIS ON ITS OWN SCORE. Six bands -- the usual five plus a narrow 400-700 Hz, because this master is tonal -- over every start at 0.5 s and every length from 28 to 42 s. The best band match in the file is a 28.5 s body from 52.50 s at 0.25 dB RMS; this one scores 0.30. The 28.5 s body was rejected because IT CLIMBS 7.3 dB FROM ITS FIRST THIRD TO ITS LAST, so every lap would be a crescendo that resets. This body runs -51.70 to -51.78 dB across the same comparison, flat to within 0.08 dB, while still holding 10.79 dB of gust inside it. The score reads two 1.5 s shoulders and cannot see a trend across the 30 s between them; see docs/ambient_loop_note.md. IT IS TONAL, LIKE THE HOWL AND UNLIKE THE FIRE. A resonance at 451 Hz sits 10.3 dB above the local spectral trend with a second at 649 Hz at +6.2, so candidates were scored on a narrow 400-700 Hz band alongside the five and the chosen crossfade was then BUILT and measured rather than reasoned about: it costs 0.50 dB in that band, against the howl's 0.46. The chosen start also happens to be the best tonal match in the file, 0.01 dB. THE JOIN SITS IN A LULL, AND THAT IS THE POINT RATHER THAN A FAULT. Measured the way the loop note's section 2 measures a seam -- crossfade region against the rest of the file -- it reads -7.54 dB, which on the fire would have meant a hole. Decomposed, it is not one: the crossfade GAINS 0.72 dB over the raw head it replaced, and the raw head is 8.09 dB under the body mean because 64.5-66.0 s is a lull in the wind, the 12th percentile of this body's own 1.5 s windows. A quiet moment is the least audible place to wrap. Measured as a linear crossfade instead the seam reads -9.11 dB against equal power's -7.54, which is the loop note's section 2 result again. A DELIVERED SPACED PAIR, not a mono-ish file: broadband the channels correlate +0.82, but per band they run +0.71, +0.84, +0.73, -0.10 and +0.03 from the bottom up -- correlated bass, decorrelated top, which is what a spaced pair looks like and what raw M/S does not. See sfx/README.md on Alms, where the same reading settled a different question.

sfx/ambient/taxation_actionA/wheat_sfx_v.design: BUILT WITH CLAUDE, not with ChatGPT as the rest of this tree's beds were, and the whole lap was authored as one mix rather than as nine independent stems: the nine summed against the reference mix at maximum absolute sample difference 0.000e+00, 0 differing samples of 2,400,000. That is why every bed here carries gainDb 0.0 -- the balance between them is baked into the stems, so an action-level move scales all nine together and cannot disturb it. A record of method, not a rights claim. NO AUDIO HERE IS MODEL OUTPUT -- every sample traces to the upload(s) in `sources`. THE LAP IS A STORY WITH TIMINGS, WRITTEN IN WORDS FIRST. It had been assembled as a set of events and read as chaotic -- the stone landed at the top, the grain answered nothing, and 14 to 22 s held one creak and eight seconds of nothing. The scene was written out in prose, then timed: grain poured, coin counted, tally notched, stone set down and accepted. IT MOVED FROM 30 s TO 25 s AND NOTHING WAS CUT TO DO IT -- the approach to the stone was compressed and the head and tail trimmed. 30 s was never a tree standard: of 137 ambient beds, 99 are 35 s and 16 are 25 s, and the only four at 30 s were this action's own. Three men at a table in a barn: a collector and two peasants, one bearing grain and one bearing stone. A tax is being paid in kind, and the twenty-five seconds is one transaction from start to finish. THE COUNT WAS WRONG IN THIS TREE'S OWN NOTES UNTIL 2026-10-20, which said four men at a table; the artwork shows three, and the error was written here and then quoted back as established fact.

sfx/ambient/allocation_actionA/wool_robe.modifications: THE CONTAINER AND NOTHING ELSE: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo. No trim, no fade, no level change, no loop made here. IT IS A PURE ADDITION TO THE APPROVED MIX, AND THAT IS AN IDENTITY RATHER THAN A CLAIM. Three arithmetic checks on the 24-bit masters, all of them exact to one least significant bit (1.19e-07): footsteps + keys = allocation_ambient_queue_v09_seamless_loop.wav; footsteps + keys + wool = allocation_v09_with_wool_preview.wav; and preview MINUS v09 = this stem with a maximum sample difference of ZERO. So nothing in the bed that was already approved has moved, and the three stems at -23.0 are the preview at -23.0, bit for bit. The earlier two-stem split could only be checked at r = +0.9970 with a residual 22.2 dB down because the composite it was checked against had been through Vorbis; with no codec anywhere in the path the floor is the 24-bit LSB, which is what these three read. ITS MATERIAL WAS TRACED BACK INTO THE SOURCE BY MEASUREMENT. 57 half-second windows of the stem loud enough to probe were cross-correlated against the whole 145.262 s upload; 13 matched decisively (r 0.33 to 0.90, and at least three times the next peak anywhere else in the recording), locating the material at about 24.4, 41.5, 46.0, 63.8-64.5 and 100.8-106.0 s. Consecutive probes map to consecutive source times at exactly 1:1, so the material is cut and placed and NOT time-stretched. The other 44 windows match nothing cleanly, which is expected and not a counter-indication: several placed copies overlap at any instant, so no single window is a scaled copy of one span. IT IS 28.500000 s TO THE SAMPLE, like both partners and like the mix they came out of. ALMOST NO STEREO WIDTH, AND THAT IS WORTH A SECOND LOOK. The side channel sits 20.4 dB under the mid and the channels correlate +0.97 FLAT ACROSS EVERY BAND (+0.977 to +0.982 from 20 Hz to 20 kHz), which is a mono source with a trace of uniform decorrelation rather than a placed field. The footsteps it is meant to belong to run +0.69, +0.88, +0.36, +0.17, +0.04, +0.01 up the bands, with the side only 3.7 dB under the mid -- several walkers at several distances. If the robes are the walkers' robes they ought to share that spread, and they do not: the feet are across the cloister and the cloth is in the middle of your head. Not a fault in the file and nothing to fix here, but it is the first thing to try in the DAW. IT HAS HOLES AND THEY ARE COVERED. 22.4% of the stem is exact digital silence in 13 spans, the longest 1.570 s at 12.30-13.87 s; the footsteps stem has NO silence anywhere, so the three summed never drop out. Alone this track would stutter. ADDING IT DOES NOT BREAK v09's WRAP, which had to be checked because the wrap was baked before this layer existed. The step across a butt join goes to 0.0004 / 0.0011, still under the preview's own median sample-to-sample difference of 0.0019 / 0.0018; the 1.5 s window straddling the wrap moves from the 17th percentile to the 16th; and the dip at the wrap deepens from 3.2 dB under the median to 4.4. Measurably worse, inaudibly so, and well inside the material's own fluctuation.

sources.note: "Six footsteps on stone with hiking boots. Each step is separated by about 250 ms of silence. Recorded with a H4n Pro on 06/06/2020." sfx/ambient/ordination_actionB/footsteps.title: Mission footsteps -- a pilgrim walking
sfx/ambient/ordination_actionB/footsteps.role: one of two tracks under ordination actionB, which is Mission: a pilgrim setting out, walking with a staff. The first bed on this duty action and the eighth folder in sfx/ambient/.
sfx/ambient/ordination_actionB/footsteps.modifications: THE CONTAINER AND NOTHING ELSE: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo. No trim, no fade, no level change, no loop made here -- it arrived looped. IT IS A REAL LOOP AND NOT MERELY A CLICKLESS ONE, WHICH ARE DIFFERENT THINGS. Both ends are exact digital silence, so the step across a butt join is 0.000000 in both channels -- and that figure means nothing, for the reason the deleted Allocation cathedral taught: silence joined to silence makes no click and is not the absence of a seam. ON A METRICAL WALK THE SEAM IS THE RHYTHM, and the rhythm holds. The 54 footfalls run at a median 0.605 s apart, which is 99.2 steps a minute against the 100 the filename claims, and THE INTERVAL ACROSS THE WRAP IS 0.600 s -- five milliseconds off the walking step. The gait continues through the loop point. Compare build_roads_actionA/rammers, whose wrap gap is 0.13 s shorter than its tightest interior pause, and build_roads_actionA/horse_snorts, whose event rate ramps across the body and resets. THE LOOP CLOSES BECAUSE THE COUNTS DIVIDE, which is worth writing down as a method. There are 54 steps and the staff lands on every third without a single exception -- steps 3, 6, 9 and so on to 54, eighteen plants, seventeen gaps all exactly three. 54 / 3 = 18 EXACTLY, so the staff comes back onto the same foot at the wrap. The footfalls do the same thing one layer down: the six source steps are cycled in a strict order and 54 / 6 = 9 EXACTLY, so the rotation also closes. Two patterns, both commensurate with the length, and no crossfade anywhere. Had there been 53 steps the staff would have changed feet every lap and no amount of wrap-window percentile would have found it. THE TWO PAUSES ARE 2.400 AND 2.405 s, five milliseconds apart, falling after the 18th and the 38th step. They are what keeps 36 s of metronome from sounding like one: the walker stops twice. The staff's every-third count carries straight through them rather than restarting, which is what makes the arithmetic above work. ITS SOURCE WAS CONFIRMED EVENT BY EVENT, at r up to 0.998. Each stem footfall was cross-correlated against each of the six source steps: stem 2.56 s matches source step 3 at 0.998, stem 0.77 matches step 4 at 0.977, stem 1.36 matches step 5 at 0.967. The rows repeat with period six -- stem 0.17 and 3.77 give identical figures -- which is how the strict rotation above was found. A NOTE ON THE METHOD, because the usual probe failed here. The sliding cross-correlation that confirmed the wind and the ox cart found NOTHING on either of these, 0 of 117 windows. It normalises each candidate position by the source's local energy with a percentile floor, and on a source that is 3.5 s of six isolated events in silence that floor clamps almost everywhere and flattens the result. On a short sparse source, compare event against event instead of sliding a window. The probe's blind spot, not the file's. THE SIX STEPS ARE HEARD NINE TIMES EACH and in the same order, so the same 3.6 s of material returns ten times across the lap. Under a staff and whatever else Mission gets, that is unlikely to read; soloed it will. The Taxation wheat record makes the same observation about 6.8 s of grain behind 30 s.

Gated it reads -34.03, 1.86 dB off the ungated figure with 231 of 357 blocks surviving, and 47.7% of the file is exact digital silence -- a walk is half air. THE TRIM IS ZERO BECAUSE NOBODY HAS SET IT, and there is no cue on this action to set it against.

sfx/ambient/ordination_actionB/rats_cros.modifications: THE SOURCE IS NAMED BY THE COVERING NOTE AND THE AUDIO DOES NOT CORROBORATE IT. This is the first bed in the tree filed in that state, and it is recorded rather than smoothed over, because the whole point of checking sources against the audio is that sometimes the check fails. WHAT WAS TRIED. Event-against-event waveform correlation, the method that placed the dogs at r = 0.999 and the first squeak at r = 0.978, reaches r = 0.074 on all four footfalls -- nothing. A pitch or speed change would destroy waveform correlation, so the source was resampled across fifteen ratios from x0.5 to x3.0 and every one re-probed: the best score anywhere in that sweep is r = 0.18, at x0.60. AND A WEAKER METHOD THAT IS NOT EVIDENCE: amplitude envelopes survive pitch shifting, and the four events score 0.65 to 0.91 against their best-matching IENBA footfall. That looks supportive and is not. The source has 120 onsets, so taking the best of 120 inflates any score, and the same test against an unrelated wooden-stick file still reaches 0.74. The method cannot tell those apart and so cannot identify anything. THE OWNER SUPPLIED THE MISSING HALF: the stem is this upload SPED UP AND LAYERED -- see `design` for by what. That is the explanation, and it also says why no amount of probing was going to find it. Layering sums several source hits into one event, so a probe compares a mixture against a single hit and the correlation falls apart however well the speed is guessed. A further sweep was run on that account -- 80 ms windows on the attacks alone, where whichever layer dominates the onset has the best chance of surviving, across sixty-one speed ratios from x1.00 to x4.00 in steps of 0.05. Best anywhere: r = 0.226. THE CONTROL IS THE FINDING. The identical sweep against deadrobotmusic's wooden stick, a file that is certainly NOT in this stem, reaches r = 0.2965 -- HIGHER than the real source scores. So the method has no discriminating power on this material at all, and the right conclusion is not that the evidence is weak but that correlation cannot speak to this file in either direction. `provenanceConfidence` stays because the audio still has not confirmed anything; what has changed is that the silence is now explained rather than open. The licence position was never at risk -- CC0 either way, and the alternatives on the owner's disk that day were CC0 or Pixabay too. THE CONTAINER: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo, no trim and no level change.

sources.note: "Slow rumble, squeak and rattle from an ox cart. Wooden wheels turning." THE OLDEST RECORDING IN THIS TREE BY A WIDE MARGIN: the uploader states these are copies of Hollywood optical and magnetic effects from the 1930s to the 1960s, transferred to full-track tape by USC Cinema and digitised without restoration, so "they have not all been restored and may have some noise". Its 2 s blocks span 4.94 dB across the whole 67.6 s and every candidate body in the search landed between -57.20 and -57.48 dBFS -- a range of 0.28 dB. Where the fire's shoulder search spread 0.70 to 11.06 dB and the sheltered wind's 0.30 to 325, this one spreads 0.37 to 6.12 and the top dozen candidates are all under 1 dB. On material this even the shoulder match stops being the thing that decides, which is worth knowing because it is the first counter-case to a rule that has held for every bed so far. SO THE LENGTH WAS CHOSEN FOR WHAT IT PLAYS AGAINST. 25.5 s against Devotion's 35 s realigns every 1785 s, half an hour; against Silversmith's 25 s, every 1275 s. Both hold, which is deliberate -- the action it belongs to was inferred rather than given, so the cut had to survive being wrong. NOTE WHAT MATCHING WOULD HAVE COST: a 35 s body scored 0.45 dB, better than several that were kept, and would have locked to Devotion on every single lap. TONAL, AND IT COST NOTHING. Excesses of 9.4 dB at 9226 Hz and 8.2 dB at 1335 Hz over the spectral trend, so both were scored as narrow bands alongside the five and the crossfade was built and measured: 0.00 dB in the 1335 Hz band and -0.04 in the 9226. The crossfade GAINS 0.38 dB over the raw head it replaced, and that raw head is 0.90 dB under the body mean -- so the single figure section 2 would give, -0.55 dB, is for once honest, because on material this steady the two terms barely differ. That is the condition under which the old measure was always right. sfx/ambient/taxation_actionA/room_sfx_v0.source: The barn around everything, continuous for the whole lap, cut from one CC0 freesound upload. IT REPLACES THE saintstereo BARN, whose own uploader's description gave the game away: it is someone climbing to the second floor of their grandmother's barn, so the footsteps at both ends are a person on a wooden staircase and the events in the middle are a squeaky pulley and a pedal-operated flywheel. Looped under the lap, that person climbed the stairs once every thirty seconds.

sources.title: DMP013016 INT BARN STORM
sources.note: Schoeps MS Ball on portable DAT, decoded to stereo -- WHICH IS WHY IT MEASURES 98.7% OF ITS SIDE ENERGY UNEXPLAINED. An MS decode puts the figure-of-eight capsule's whole output in the side signal, so a least-squares fit of side to mid finds nothing, and the number means the recording is genuinely two microphones rather than one widened. The uploader calls it roomtone of the interior of a barn, with wind outside, which is exactly what the bed is used as.

Its join was clean by every measure the check applied -- the sample step across the wrap was 1.7x the median adjacent step, well inside tolerance -- and the head was 3.09 dB quieter than the tail. The check had never compared LEVEL across the seam, only continuity, and a 3 dB step in a continuous bed is heard as the bed breathing once a lap. The metric is now part of the check. A GAIN RAMP WAS TRIED AND DISCARDED. Correcting the level into the existing window is the obvious repair and it does not work: a ramp's endpoints do not meet, and the corrected build measured a wrap step 5.7x the median -- it traded an audible level step for an audible click. The window was reselected for continuity across the seam instead, which is the slower answer and the right one. NARROWED A SECOND TIME AFTER ENCODING: the first encode folded -1.010 dB at 2 kHz, over the limit, so a small extra narrowing was applied and the file re-encoded. The silence mask does not apply to this bed -- it has no silence to protect.

The table takes the load at 17.500, the block lands at 17.550, and at 19.240 it is shoved square. Between 18.250 and 19.240 nothing sounds but `room` -- a protected silence, and the lap's only one. THE PREVIOUS ARRANGEMENT PUT THIS AT THE TOP OF THE LAP and it read as chaotic: the heaviest thing in the scene arriving before anything had been established. It is now the last event but one.
sfx/ambient/taxation_actionA/stone_block.modifications: Three elements placed, side-scaled, and panned. Resampled 44.1 -> 48 kHz, Vorbis q6. No trim, no reverb, no compression, no pitch or time processing. 89.9% exact digital silence. THE SIDE-SCALE IS THE FOLD REPAIR AND IT IS NOT COSMETIC: shove side x 0.22, placement side x 0.70, then a further x 0.70 on the whole bed before the pan. Without it the bed folds -4.463 dB whole and -5.937 dB at 500 Hz. PANNED BY PULLING THE LEFT CHANNEL DOWN, NOT BY RAISING THE RIGHT. Its peak is -2.59 dBFS, the loudest in the action; a symmetric pan to 5.3 dB right would reach +0.43 dBFS and clip. Attenuating one channel leaves the peak exactly where it is. AN EARLIER TEST BUILD DISTORTED THE IMPACT and the cause is worth keeping: it cut 0.300 s from 0.830 instead of the length the spec meant, which pulled in a forbidden bounce at 1.085 s and chopped a tail still at -36 dBFS straight into digital silence, a step of 3.6e-03. The run is 0.830 to 1.080 with a 50 ms fade; the last sample before silence is 3.6e-06. The ambiguity was real and was in the spec, not in the reading of it.

NARROWER THAN ITS TARGET BY ABOUT 2 dB -- the layout asks -10 to -12 de-panned and this sits at -13.97, which is the side-scale repair's cost and is reported rather than recovered. ONE THING FAILS AND NO GUARD MEASURES IT: a 450 ms window around the landing folds -1.259 dB at 500 Hz in the finished mix. Neither narrowing nor repositioning reaches it -- halving the side signal moves it 0.4 dB and shifting the pan 1.8 dB moves it 0.14 dB -- because the side energy in that band is intrinsic to the recording. A prediction that narrowing would bring it inside 1 dB was made here and was wrong; it is recorded because the wrong prediction is the useful part. The bed, the lap and the shove all pass. sfx/ambient/build_roads_actionB/tinkerin.modifications: ALL FOUR SOURCES CONFIRMED, AND NOT BY CORRELATION -- BY RECONSTRUCTION. The project owner supplied `build_shrine_tinkering_more_stem_v01_25s_creation_notes.md`, which specifies the whole chain: which channel of each source, resample_poly ratios, a 70 Hz and a 6,500 Hz second-order Butterworth applied with causal sosfilt to the WHOLE source before cutting, the exact sample slice of each excerpt, raised-cosine edge fades, an equal-power pan at -0.10 (L x0.7604059656000309, R x0.6494480483301837), and a start frame and gain for each of twelve cues. REBUILT FROM THAT RECIPE, EVERY ONE OF THE TWELVE MATCHES THE STEM AT r = +1.000000 ON BOTH CHANNELS, fitted gain +1.0000, with the residual 101 to 107 dB under the stem -- which is the triangular dither floor the notes say was applied at quantization. That is not a trace, it is a reproduction: this is now the best-evidenced bed in the tree by a wide margin, and the only one whose audio can be regenerated from first principles. THE FOUR SOURCE FINGERPRINTS IN THE NOTES MATCH THE FILES ON DISK, and so does the export fingerprint of the stem itself, 27877fa12828b9ff... . THE NOTES' OWN MEASUREMENTS AGREE WITH THIS TREE'S: true peak -11.55 against -11.58 measured here, sample peak about -11.75 against -11.73, and the notes' `integrated loudness` of -37.25 is the GATED figure, which reads -37.16 here; this tree records ungated, -42.09, and the two are different measures rather than a disagreement. WHAT THE FIRST PASS GOT WRONG, KEPT BECAUSE THE FAULT IS GENERAL. Probing the stem against the RAW sources confirmed three of the four and left the brick at `stated-not-corroborated` for about an hour. Two independent mistakes, both mine. FIRST, THE SOURCES ARE FILTERED BEFORE THEY ARE CUT. A 6,500 Hz low-pass takes more from a 0.42 s brick contact, which is mostly broadband transient, than from a rock drag or a slab, whose energy already sits low -- so the same probe that scored 0.92 on the drags scored an unstable 0.585 on the brick, and flipped sign when the window length changed. A PROBE AGAINST AN UNPROCESSED SOURCE IS A PROBE AGAINST SOMETHING THE STEM DOES NOT CONTAIN. SECOND, AND WORSE, THE TEST I TRUSTED MOST WAS THE BROKEN ONE. `If one recording is used three times, the three uses correlate with each other` is sound, and it needs no source at all -- but I ran it at FIXED ALIGNMENT and it returned +0.159, +0.159 and -0.042, which I read as proof the three runs were different sounds. Allowing a lag search returns r = +1.0000 at lags of -1.00, +1.00 and +2.00 ms. The three runs are bit-identical gestures. THE 1-2 MS IS ITSELF EXPLAINED BY THE RECIPE: the three brick cues carry different gains, -14.23, -14.73 and -14.93 dB, so each one's 4 ms raised-cosine fade-in crosses the 24-bit quantization threshold at a different moment, and a silence detector reports three different onsets for three identical gestures. A SELF-SIMILARITY TEST MUST CROSS-CORRELATE, NEVER COMPARE AT A FIXED OFFSET, and on a transient one millisecond is the difference between 1.00 and 0.15. THE CONTAINER: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo, no trim, no fade and no level change; the stem peaks at -11.7 dBFS so there was no headroom problem to solve.

sfx/ambient/produce_actionA/sickle_cutti.modifications: FORTY OF FORTY RUNS MATCH, UP TO r = 0.9015, AND THEY COME FROM ONLY TWO PLACES. Every sounding run in the stem was cross-correlated against the resampled source -- lag search, never a fixed offset, which on a source reused this heavily is not optional. All forty land at |r| >= 0.5, and their source positions collapse into just TWO distinct regions: 0.0439-0.9580 s and 1.1352-4.0603 s, 3.839 s in total, 59.9% of a 6.409 s recording. Forty placements out of under four seconds of material is the densest reuse in this tree by a wide margin; `combined` here means one short recording worked very hard. THE OVERLAP CHECK WAS RUN AGAINST ALL FIVE EXISTING BEDS IN THE FOLDER, as it now is for any stem whose name says combined. The highest figure anywhere is 0.2933, against straw_workers_sfx_v01.ogg. THAT IS THE LARGEST BED-TO-BED NUMBER THIS FOLDER HAS PRODUCED and it is reported rather than rounded away: it is roughly four times the 0.069-0.084 the straw pair scored against each other, and the reason is that both beds are dry plant matter being handled, so they genuinely resemble one another. It is still nowhere near sharing samples -- a shared excerpt returns r near 1.0 at some lag, not 0.29 -- so the conclusion is the same and the margin is simply smaller. RESAMPLING COST ALMOST NOTHING, WHICH WAS NOT THE PREDICTION. This is the only source here that needed 44.1 -> 48 kHz conversion, and conversion between the project's chain and this probe's ffmpeg resampler is exactly the kind of processing distance that has lowered every other trace. It reaches 0.90, HIGHER than sheaf_handling's 0.81 and straw_workers' 0.50-0.74, both cut from a source already at 48 kHz. That is the second time in two days the processing-distance rule has failed to predict an ordering, after stalk_brushing, and the two failures agree with each other: THE RULE DESCRIBES A TENDENCY AND MUST NOT BE USED TO RANK. THE CONTAINER: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo, no trim, no fade and no level change; the stem peaks at -14.2 dBFS so there was no headroom problem to solve.
sfx/ambient/produce_actionA/sickle_cutti.measured: 35000 ms, peak -14.2 dB, integrated -39.86 LUFS, true peak -14.06 dBTP, stereo 48 kHz, L/R correlation +0.969711. IT IS THE LOUDEST BED IN PRODUCE WHEAT BY PEAK AND THE THIRD QUIETEST BY LOUDNESS, which is this folder's third peak-versus-loudness disagreement and the sharpest: at -14.06 dBTP it is 1.87 dB above the wind, and at -39.86 LUFS it is 6.03 dB below it. A blade transient is loud and brief; weather is quiet and continuous. 29.2% of the file is exact digital silence in 17 runs and material runs 1.015 to 33.353 s. Gated it reads -36.35 LUFS, 3.51 dB off the ungated figure on 154 of 347 blocks, against 10*log10(347/154) = 3.53 -- the block-count identity, out by 0.021 dB. THE WRAP IS SAFE OUTRIGHT: fifteen interior pauses, the longest 2.112 s, against a wrap gap of 2.661 -- 1.26x. THE FIRST DRAFT CALLED THAT THE NARROWEST PASS IN THE TREE AND IT IS SEVENTH OF THIRTEEN. The full ordering, computed rather than recalled: barn_creaks 1.03, ox_breathing 1.04, gallows_rope 1.10, oil_lamp_rattle 1.12, rosary 1.13, far_work 1.18, THIS BED 1.26, monk_robe 1.57, distant_dogs 1.83, crows_ravens 2.00, straw_workers 2.06, sheaf_handling 2.58, distant_rooster 7.68 -- thirteen passing outright, twelve of which loop. THAT IS THE THIRD SUPERLATIVE THIS TREE HAS GOT WRONG IN TWO DAYS by reading prose instead of computing a population, after the outright-pass count and the mono-fold cost. The pattern is not carelessness about a particular fact, it is a method: a claim of the form `most` or `only` is a claim about every file, and every file is cheap to check. Both ends are true digital silence and the butt-join step is 0.000000 on both channels. VORBIS COLLAPSED 452 RUNS INTO 17, which is the crows' lesson again and in its largest absolute form. The WAV stem holds 452 separate non-silent runs at 31.81% silence; the shipped .ogg holds SEVENTEEN at 29.18%, because the encoder rings out across hundreds of sub-100 ms gaps between blade strokes. The crows' 374 to 4 is still the larger RATIO, 93x against 27x, but 452 is the largest stem run count recorded here, and the direction is the same one every file has shown: the shipped asset is less silent than the stem it came from. A RUN COUNT READ OFF A STEM DESCRIBES THE EDIT, NOT THE ASSET. IT IS NOT A MONO SIGNAL PANNED, AND THAT WAS PREDICTED RATHER THAN OBSERVED. straw_workers' record proposed that a bed fits an exact scalar if it is built from one source region panned once, and cannot if it has several gestures at several pans. This bed has forty placements, so the prediction was that it would not fit; measured in the WAV stem it gives R = 0.4410 x L with an 18.37% residual. Three exact and three loose now, and the rule has been tested once since it was written and held. Folding to mono costs 2.86 dB and the best inter-channel lag is +0.000 ms, so there is no Haas widener. THE TRIM IS ZERO BECAUSE NOBODY HAS SET IT.

sfx/ambient/produce_actionB/distant_owl_.title: Produce Stone distant owl -- one dusk call across the quarry
sfx/ambient/produce_actionB/distant_owl_.role: The fifth track of seventeen under produce actionB, which is Produce Stone. It loops. A single owl call at 20.4 s. THE ONLY TRACK IN THIS FOLDER WHOSE SOURCE A DIRECT PROBE COULD NOT SUPPORT -- it was carried for a day as stated-not-corroborated and then confirmed, first by high-passing both sides and then by rebuilding it from the stated recipe; see `modifications`, which keeps the failed trace rather than replacing it. IT DOES NOT LOOP -- see `loop`. FILED loop: false ON 2026-10-18.
sfx/ambient/produce_actionB/distant_owl_.modifications: THE DIRECT TRACE FAILED, THE RECORD SAID SO FOR A DAY, AND THEN THE FAILURE TURNED OUT TO BE THE PROBE'S. The bed's single sounding run is 20.364-25.420 s, which is 5.056 s -- 1.1% LONGER THAN THE WHOLE SOURCE. Probed against the resampled source it reaches r = 0.0337 where the moth control reaches 0.0308: no separation at all. A SPEED SEARCH WAS RUN ON THE SUSPICION THAT THE CALL HAD BEEN STRETCHED, resampling the source across factors from 0.90 to 1.10; every factor scored at or below 0.0408, with the best at 1.10 and no peak near the 1.011 the duration mismatch implies. So it is not a simple stretch either. THREE EXPLANATIONS WERE OPEN AT THAT POINT -- processing far beyond anything else in this tree, a different recording, or a different take -- AND THE REAL ANSWER WAS A FOURTH NOBODY HAD LOOKED FOR: THE PROBE WAS NOT MEASURING THE OWL. 97.76% OF THE SOURCE FILE'S ENERGY SITS BELOW 20 Hz, inaudible rumble, 29% of it below 5 Hz; the hoot itself is 0.22% of the file. Normalised cross-correlation divides by total energy, so it was scoring the rumble against a bed whose chain had high-passed that rumble away, and 0.0337 was the honest answer to the wrong question. The owl is the most subsonic-dominated source behind this folder by a factor of thirty-four: all eighteen source entries were measured and the next worst is the quarry wind's breeze at 2.85%, then dragging at 1.68% and the stone crash at 1.33%. HIGH-PASS BOTH SIDES AT 100 Hz AND THE SAME PROBE RETURNS r = 0.9974. THEN IT WAS RECONSTRUCTED RATHER THAN TRACED, which is the stronger test: the project owner supplied the chain -- full 5 s source at original pitch and speed, placed at 20.40 s, panned to about +0.48 with the stereo width narrowed to 40%, high-passed near 120 Hz and low-passed near 4.3 kHz, two distance reflections at ~120 ms / 5.5% and ~230 ms / 2.5%, peak set to about -24 dBFS, 35 ms fade in and 280 ms fade out -- and the rebuild reproduces the shipped bed at r = +0.9966 LAG-SEARCHED, WITH 0.0 ms OF DRIFT, landing at 20.3640 s. At the stated placement with no search at all it is +0.9880. THE TWO DISCREPANCIES THAT STARTED THIS BOTH FALL OUT OF THE REBUILD: the run begins 36 ms before the stated 20.400 because Vorbis rings backwards into the silence ahead of a transient, and it ends at 25.420 against the rebuild's 25.630 because the last 210 ms of the fade-out lies under the encoder's resolution. The 5.056 s run is longer than the 5.000 s source because the reflections extend the tail, not because anything was stretched -- which is also why the speed search found no peak. THE LESSON IS WRITTEN INTO THE TOOL: `provenance.py` now computes `subsonic_fraction()` and warns when a source is dominated by energy no audible chain would keep, and `tests/action_board/test_provenance.py` holds a case that fails on a buried source and passes once high-passed. A LOW r IS A STATEMENT ABOUT THE PROBE AS MUCH AS ABOUT THE FILE. The licence was never in question -- the upload is CC0 and so is everything else here. THE CONTAINER: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo, no trim, no fade, no level change. FILED loop: false. THE CALL SITS 21.4 s INTO A 35 s FILE and runs 1.26 s, with nothing before it and 10.1 s of silence after -- a 31.2 s gap across the wrap. Looping it gave an owl calling to a metronome: the same 1.26 s recording, at the same offset, every 35 seconds, and it is the most exposed thing in the folder because it is one recognisable animal with silence on both sides and nothing to mask it. The flag costs the other half of the trade and that was accepted knowingly: the call now arrives once, 21.4 s after the action is selected, so a player who moves on sooner never hears it and a player who stays hears it once. Mission's door_close, Produce Wheat's distant_rooster and Allocation's three mouse stems carry the same flag for the same reason. THE FILE WAS NOT RETIMED: moving the call to 00:00 would make it a one-shot that fires on the click, which reads as a response to the click rather than as weather. `quarry_hoist_sfx_v02.ogg` is the same shape and is still looping.

sfx/ambient/produce_actionB/debris_cleav.modifications: SOURCE CONFIRMED AND ONE OF THEM IS THE GAME'S OWN CUE. The rock impacts land at r up to 0.9978 on five of six windows, which is the cleanest trace in this folder. The cue itself lands at 0.9889 on one window, confirming the manifest's claim that it was used. THE CUE BEING INSIDE THE BED HAS A CONSEQUENCE NOBODY HAS DECIDED ON YET: when a player confirms Produce Stone, the cue fires over an ambience that already contains it, so the two will reinforce rather than separate. That is the exact masking case the generic-cue discussion turned on, and it is now a measured fact about this action rather than a worry. A CONTROL THAT LOOKED LIKE A MISSING SOURCE AND WAS NOT, RESOLVED 2026-10-18. discofield's stone crash, run here as a control because the manifest lists it only under power_strikes, reached 0.5550 on one window and was filed as a likely manifest omission. IT IS THE SHORT-RUN ARTEFACT AND NOTHING ELSE. That window is a 65 ms run at 26.131-26.196 s, well under the 150 ms below which this tree has measured that nothing discriminates -- and THE CUE SCORES 0.4079 ON THE SAME WINDOW, which it cannot be doing honestly, because the cue's real placement is a 1.57 s run at 9.176 s where it reaches 0.9889. Two checks settle it: the cue and discofield's crash, correlated against each other whole and lag-searched, reach only 0.0850, so they are not the same recording; and subtracting the cue's fitted contribution from its own run moves discofield from 0.1225 to 0.1495, so they are independent. THE MANIFEST IS CORRECT and this bed has two sources. The rule that explains it was established on produce_actionA/nearby_raven four hours before this figure was filed, and was not applied because the trace script reported a maximum across runs without checking how long the winning run was -- A THRESHOLD IS ONLY WORTH HAVING IF THE TOOL APPLIES IT, and sfx_lab/provenance.py now flags short runs in its own output. THE CONTAINER: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo, no trim, no fade, no level change. THE REASON GIVEN FOR TAKING IT OUT WAS WRONG, AND THE ERROR WAS THIS TREE'S, NOT THE SUPPLIER'S. The board does not play per-action cues. It plays one generic select and one generic confirm from `general/<CUE_SET>_<slot>`, which is what `CUE_SET = "set3"` selects, and `duty_actions/` is walked by `bundled_art()` for ARTWORK ONLY -- no audio in that folder reaches a player in this build. The doubling this change was made to prevent cannot happen and has not been possible since the board moved to generic cues. The prose that said otherwise predates that move and was read as current on 2026-10-18.

sfx/ambient/produce_actionB/debris_cleav.modifications: THE CUE IS OUT, AND IT SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN. v01 carried `produce_actionB_sfx_v02.ogg` -- the action's own cue -- inside the ambience at r 0.9889, so confirming Produce Stone fired the cue over a bed that already held it and the two reinforced rather than separated. The cleave is now built from rock only: Nox_Sound's impacts with discofield's stone crash as the large event. MEASURED AGAINST THE CUE AT A MATCHED RATE -- the cue is 96 kHz and this is 48, and correlating them as if they shared a rate is a mistake this tree has already made once -- v01 reads 0.99 and this reads 0.55 on a 200 ms window, 0.43 on 500 ms and 0.42 on 1.22 s. WINDOWS BELOW 150 ms ARE NOT QUOTED because this tree has measured that nothing discriminates there. THE RESIDUAL IS NOT THE CUE, IT IS DISCOFIELD: v01's own record already logged the stone crash as a control hit at 0.5550 on this bed, so what replaced the cue is a different recording that happens to resemble it. The supplier reported 0.285 for the same comparison; that figure is not reproducible here and the supplier holds no copy of the cue to have measured it against. THE CLEAVE IS 6.78 dB ABOVE THE NEXT EVENT IN ITS OWN STEM, which breaks the delivery contract's 4 dB rule and is a declared exception: it is the event the bed exists for. THE CONTAINER: Vorbis q6 at the stem's own 48 kHz stereo, no trim, no fade, no level change. The container's last granule is exactly 1,680,000 samples, so the board's loopEnd is 35.000 s and not the padded decode length. THE REASON GIVEN FOR TAKING IT OUT WAS WRONG, AND THE ERROR WAS THIS TREE'S, NOT THE SUPPLIER'S. The board does not play per-action cues. It plays one generic select and one generic confirm from `general/<CUE_SET>_<slot>`, which is what `CUE_SET = "set3"` selects, and `duty_actions/` is walked by `bundled_art()` for ARTWORK ONLY -- no audio in that folder reaches a player in this build. The doubling this change was made to prevent cannot happen and has not been possible since the board moved to generic cues. The prose that said otherwise predates that move and was read as current on 2026-10-18. THIS STEM IS THEREFORE PENDING REPLACEMENT: v17 restores the v14 cascade with v15's room, and what was lost is not level or spectrum -- those matched to within 0.04 dB RMS and 0.6 dB in every octave band -- but the shape in time. v14 built into its peak over 0.34 s and was followed by half a second of debris at -12 to -17 dB; this arrives at full level at once and decays into a wash at -24 to -35 dB. Same energy, different event.

slotFoldersNote: Which folder under duty_actions/ holds each duty action's pictures. IT CANNOT BE DERIVED and that is why it is written down: Clerical's actionA is `gain_piety` and its actionB `gain_coins`, while Produce's actionA is `gain_wheat` and its actionB `gain_stone` -- so neither alphabetical order nor the action's own name in duty_text.json gives the answer. It lives HERE rather than in duty_text.json because that file is the wording and says so; a folder is a fact about this tree, which is what this file is already about (see assetDirs). A duty with one action has one entry: Taxation and Allocation each have one, and the folders that were left over from before the wording existed -- taxation/action_b and allocation/special_activity -- are stale. ui/board_v2/action_board reads this when a picture lands in a slot that has none yet, and refuses to guess when a slot is missing from it.
nonSlotFoldersNote: Folders under a duty that are NOT one of its actions. Every tool that walks duty_actions/ has to skip them, and until this key existed each one carried its own copy of the word 'masters' -- so when 'seals' appeared, the action board was taught about it and the layout lab was not, and the layout lab quietly drew a 78px wax seal as Clerical's 590x295 action card. One list, read by every walk.  `cutouts` joined this list the moment the folder existed, and NOT when it joins markFolders. The two lists answer different questions: markFolders is where a tile's mark may be drawn from, and this is which folders under a duty are not one of its two actions. A cutout is not an action either way. Leaving it out cost five action cards -- taxation, both Build Roads and both Construct -- which quietly drew a 68px emblem stretched across 590 x 295, because the cards' folders are walked in sorted order and `cutouts` lands after `action_a`, `build_road` and `construct_building` and overwrote them. The five that survived did so only because their folder names sort after the letter c.
imageSuffixesNote: Extensions an image in this tree may carry, for the walks that look for one. The SHIPPED prints are WebP at quality 90 -- 40 MB of PNG became 7 MB for a worst-case difference of 12 of 255 on one pixel, measured on the seal composited over its tile at the size the board actually inlines. The MASTERS stay PNG: they are the archive, and a lossy archive is not one. Three generators and the tests look for images here, so the list lives in one place rather than four.
defaultProvenance: UNLESS AN ENTRY SAYS OTHERWISE, AN IMAGE IN THIS TREE WAS GENERATED WITH ChatGPT (OpenAI) and carries the openai-generated licence. That is the project's stated default for artwork, not a guess made per file: anything with a different origin -- a third-party icon, a hand-drawn asset, deterministic script output -- has to say so in its own entry, because the default would otherwise quietly mislabel it. A new image added here with no entry at all is a gap, not an implicit default; tests/layout_lab/test_board_v2_attribution.py fails on one.
markFoldersNote: Folders under a duty that hold the small mark drawn in its tile, IN ORDER OF PRECEDENCE: when a slot has a mark in more than one of them, the LAST one listed is the one the board draws. That ordering is load-bearing and it is not derivable. A version number counts up inside one lineage and means nothing across two, so comparing a seal's v02 with an icon's v01 is comparing unrelated counters -- which is exactly what the board did for one build, leaving eleven slots drawing wax discs with their icons already filed beside them. Within a folder the highest version still wins. `seals` was the only folder and its name was typed into both tools that READ the tree -- the action board and the duty art lab; `icons` arrived the day a mark was not a wax disc, and a second place to list it is exactly how one of them would have been missed, which is what happened the last time, when `seals` itself appeared and the layout lab was never told and drew a 78px wax seal as a 590x295 action card. The folder also says what kind of thing the mark is. That is NOT the same question as a file's `ground`, which says whose ground it is drawn on; the two agree today because the only cut-outs so far are the only icons so far, and they will not always. tools/duty_art/file_seals.py is deliberately NOT on this list: it makes wax seals -- it scales each one to the discs' 0.906 of its square and re-encodes the print as WebP -- so `seals` is simply the right answer for it, and teaching it to choose would let a cut-out through a correction meant for a disc. Cut-outs are framed in ui/board_v2/icon_lab/ instead.
ambientFoldersNote: A BED LIVES IN A FOLDER NAMED AFTER THE DUTY ACTION IT PLAYS UNDER -- sfx/ambient/<duty>_<slot>/, the same string the action's own cue is named with, so sfx/ambient/taxation_actionA/ sits beside sfx/duty_actions/taxation_actionA_sfx_v01.ogg. IT USED TO BE THE FILENAME'S JOB. A flat sfx/ambient/ resolved a bed to its action by dropping trailing words off the stem until one matched a duty action's name, so `allocation_wind` found Allocation. That works for two tracks and stops working for four: a stem wants a name that says what it IS -- wheat, coins, barn creaks -- and those names collide across actions the moment two duties both have wheat in them. The folder now owns which action, the filename owns which track, and neither repeats the other. Unlike slotFolders above, this one IS derivable and is not a mapping: the folder name is the duty key and the slot joined by an underscore, and the generator refuses a folder that does not name a real duty action rather than guessing.
ambientMasterNote: THE ONE GAIN THE WHOLE BOARD PASSES THROUGH, and it is arithmetic rather than taste. The loudest action after its group trim is clerical_actionA at -3.60 dBTP. An equal-power crossfade holds both actions at 0.7071 through the middle of a switch, so two whose peaks coincide reach 1.4142 times one of them, and the confirm cue can land on top of that. THE CUE FIGURE WAS WRONG WHEN THIS NOTE WAS FIRST WRITTEN -- it said 0.7 x -0.30 dBFS, a peak no cue in this tree has ever had; the Kenney confirm it meant peaks at -1.26. The board now plays general/set3_confirm at -1.38 dBFS, so the cue reaches 0.7 x -1.38 = -4.48 dBFS. At -4.5 dB the worst case comes to -0.80 dBFS, which is the point: the bound is PROVABLE rather than probable, and clipping that only happens when three peaks coincide is the kind nobody reproduces and everybody hears. It costs 4.5 dB of a board whose loudest moment is otherwise 3.6 dB under full scale, so it costs nothing worth keeping. RECOMPUTE IT WHEN THE TRIMS ARE SET, AND WHEN THE CUE SET CHANGES: the figure follows the loudest action and the loudest cue, not the other way round. It was rechecked against set3 on 2026-10-18 and -4.5 still held, which is the only reason it did not move.
ambientGroupsNote: A SECOND LEVEL, ONE PER DUTY ACTION, AND IT IS A MIX PARAMETER RATHER THAN PROVENANCE. Each bed's own `gainDb` is its balance against the other beds of its action; `groupDb` here is where that whole action sits against the other actions. The two multiply: a track is heard at gainDb + groupDb. WHY TWO NUMBERS INSTEAD OF ONE. Folding a group move back into each track's gainDb gives the same sound once and then throws the structure away -- there is no longer an action level to revisit, only N numbers that happened to move together, and the next adjustment is N slider moves again. Kept apart, balancing within an action and matching actions to each other stay separate jobs, which is how they are actually done. THE GROUP CANNOT CHANGE THE BALANCE INSIDE AN ACTION, BY CONSTRUCTION. On the bench it is one gain node that every track of the action feeds, so it scales all of them by the same factor; it is not added into each track's gain, where a clamp or a rounding could pull one of them out of line. Anything that plays these beds must do the same: per-track gain, then one bus gain per action. summedTruePeakDbtp IS A RENDERED MEASUREMENT, NOT A SUM OF PEAKS -- the action's beds mixed at their trims and measured, which on Build Roads reads -3.05 dBTP where adding the individual peaks says +1.86. It scales exactly with groupDb, so the bench shows summedTruePeakDbtp + groupDb and that figure is exact rather than pessimistic. IT GOES STALE WHEN ANY TRIM MOVES, so `summedAtTrims` fingerprints the gainDb values it was computed from and a test refuses the pair when they disagree; `python3 ui/board_v2/sfx_lab/sfx_levels.py --groups --write` recomputes both. THE BOARD PLAYS THESE NOW, through generate_action_board.py's bundled_beds(), and it applies both numbers the way this note requires: one gain node per bed for `gainDb`, then ONE node per action for `groupDb`, then `ambientMaster`. THE NUMBERS BELOW ARE PROVISIONAL AND MEANT TO BE OVERWRITTEN. They were not authored; each was set to bring its action's `summedLoudnessLufs` to the median action, -33.83, rounded to half a decibel and clamped at 12 dB, so that selecting one duty action after another is not a lottery while 35 of the 63 beds still carry gainDb 0.0. A FLOOR TO START FROM, NOT A MIX -- and matching integrated loudness is not the same as matching how loud two places feel, which is the judgement the trims exist for.
